title: Standard form and orders of magnitude
summary: [[standard-form|Standard form]] writes a number as a number from 1 to just under 10, times a power of 10, such as $3.06 \times 10^{-5}$. It keeps huge and tiny numbers short and easy to compare. You'll convert numbers, calculate with them by hand, and write calculator output the way examiners accept.

goals.text: Write a number in [[standard-form|standard form]] $a \times 10^{k}$, and back again.
Compare the sizes, or [[order-of-magnitude|orders of magnitude]], of two numbers.
Multiply, divide, raise to powers and square-root numbers in standard form by hand.
Add and subtract numbers in standard form by matching their powers of 10.
Turn a calculator display such as 7.4E-6 into $7.4 \times 10^{-6}$.

synonyms: a times 10 to the power k

before.hint: When you multiply powers of the same number, add the indices.
Raising a power to a power multiplies the indices.
A negative index means one over the positive power: $10^{-3} = \frac{1}{10^{3}}$.
before.explain: $10^{-3} = \frac{1}{1000} = 0.001$. A negative power makes a number small, not negative.

blocks.text: The Earth's mass is about $5\,970\,000\,000\,000\,000\,000\,000\,000$ kg. Counting those zeros is slow, and one slip changes the size completely. [[standard-form|Standard form]] writes the digits once and lets a power of 10 carry the size: $5.97 \times 10^{24}$ kg.

blocks.statement: A number is in standard form when it is written as $a \times 10^{k}$, with $1 \le a < 10$ and $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ (a positive or negative whole number, or zero).
blocks.plain: One non-zero digit before the point, then a power of 10 saying how far to move the point.

blocks.text: 1. Put the decimal point just after the first non-zero digit. This gives $a$, the front number.
2. Count the places the point moved. That is the size of $k$.
3. For a number of 10 or more, $k > 0$. For a number below 1, $k < 0$. From 1 to just under 10, $k = 0$.

blocks.alt: In 0.0000306 the decimal point hops 5 places right to sit after the 3, giving 3.06 times 10 to the power minus 5. In 4070000000 the point hops 9 places left from the end to sit after the 4, giving 4.07 times 10 to the power 9.

blocks.question: A speck of dust has a mass of $0.000\,030\,6$ g. Write this mass in standard form.
steps: The first non-zero digit is the $3$, so $a = 3.06$.
The point moves from just after the first $0$ to just after the $3$: $5$ places right. The mass is less than $1$, so $k = -5$.
Check by going back: moving the point in $3.06$ five places left gives $0.000\,030\,6$.

blocks.text: To go back, move the point $k$ places: right if $k > 0$, left if $k < 0$. So $8.1 \times 10^{3} = 8100$ and $2.6 \times 10^{-4} = 0.000\,26$.

blocks.question: Write $52.8 \times 10^{-7}$ in standard form.
steps: $52.8$ is bigger than $10$, so this is not yet standard form. Write $52.8 = 5.28 \times 10^{1}$.
Substitute and add the powers: $5.28 \times 10^{1} \times 10^{-7} = 5.28 \times 10^{1 + (-7)} = 5.28 \times 10^{-6}$.
The front number got $10$ times smaller, so the power went up by $1$.

blocks.prompt: The Sun is about $149\,600\,000$ km from the Earth. Write this distance in standard form, in km.
blocks.hint: Put the point just after the $1$. How many places did it move?
blocks.explain: The point moves from the end of $149\,600\,000$ to just after the $1$: $8$ places left. Counting all $9$ digits gives $10^{9}$, which is $10$ times too big.

blocks.text: The power $k$ is the number's [[order-of-magnitude|order of magnitude]]: each step up in $k$ makes a number about $10$ times bigger. So compare powers first, and compare front numbers only when the powers match. With negative powers, $-6$ is bigger than $-7$.

blocks.hint: Compare the powers of $10$ first. Which is bigger, $-6$ or $-7$?

blocks.text: Calculators show very large or small answers in a short form such as 7.4E-6, where E means times $10$ to the power of the number after it.
Copying 7.4E-6 onto your paper. Examiners don't accept it: write $7.4 \times 10^{-6}$.
You can multiply in any order, so group the front numbers and the powers of $10$: $(3 \times 10^{4}) \times (2 \times 10^{5}) = (3 \times 2) \times 10^{4+5} = 6 \times 10^{9}$.
If the new front number lands outside 1 to 10, rewrite it. $30 = 3 \times 10^{1}$ pushes the power up by $1$. $0.3 = 3 \times 10^{-1}$ pulls it down by $1$.

blocks.question: Work out $(7.5 \times 10^{6}) \times (4 \times 10^{-9})$. Give your answer in [[standard-form|standard form]].
steps: Group the front numbers and the powers: $(7.5 \times 4) \times (10^{6} \times 10^{-9})$.
Multiply the front numbers: $7.5 \times 4 = 30$.
Add the powers: $6 + (-9) = -3$. So you have $30 \times 10^{-3}$.
$30$ is not less than $10$. Write $30 = 3 \times 10^{1}$, so $30 \times 10^{-3} = 3 \times 10^{1 - 3} = 3 \times 10^{-2}$.
Check with ordinary numbers: $7\,500\,000 \times 0.000\,000\,004 = 0.03$, which is $3 \times 10^{-2}$.

blocks.question: Work out $\dfrac{1.2 \times 10^{5}}{4 \times 10^{-3}}$. Give your answer in standard form.
steps: Split the fraction into two parts: $\frac{1.2}{4} \times \frac{10^{5}}{10^{-3}}$.
Divide the front numbers: $\frac{1.2}{4} = 0.3$.
Subtract the powers: $5 - (-3) = 8$. So you have $0.3 \times 10^{8}$.

blocks.text: Losing the sign when you subtract a negative power. $10^{5} \div 10^{-3} = 10^{5 - (-3)} = 10^{8}$, not $10^{2}$. Write the subtraction out with brackets.

blocks.hint: Multiply $8 \times 5$ and add the powers. Then check that the front number is less than $10$.

blocks.text: To raise a number in standard form to a power, raise both parts. The power of $10$ is multiplied, because $(10^{m})^{n} = 10^{mn}$.

blocks.question: A salt crystal is a cube with edges $5 \times 10^{-4}$ m long. Find the volume of the crystal in $\text{m}^{3}$. Give your answer in standard form.
steps: A cube's volume is its edge cubed (prior-learning section of the booklet): $V = (5 \times 10^{-4})^{3}$.
Fix the front number: $125 = 1.25 \times 10^{2}$, so $V = 1.25 \times 10^{2 - 12} = 1.25 \times 10^{-10}$.
Sense check: a half-millimetre edge gives a tiny volume, so a large negative power fits.

blocks.text: Cubing only the power of $10$. The $5$ is cubed too, giving $125$, and $(10^{-4})^{3} = 10^{-12}$: multiply the powers, don't add them.
For a square root, halve the power of $10$. If the power is odd, first move one factor of $10$ into the front number: $\sqrt{2.5 \times 10^{-7}} = \sqrt{25 \times 10^{-8}} = 5 \times 10^{-4}$.

blocks.prompt: Work out $\sqrt{8.1 \times 10^{7}}$ without a calculator. Give your answer in standard form.
blocks.hint: The power $7$ is odd. Rewrite $8.1 \times 10^{7}$ as $81$ times an even power of $10$ first.
blocks.explain: $8.1 \times 10^{7} = 81 \times 10^{6}$. Then $\sqrt{81} = 9$ and $\sqrt{10^{6}} = 10^{3}$, so the root is $9 \times 10^{3}$, which is $9000$.

blocks.text: Adding works differently: $2 \times 10^{3} + 5 \times 10^{2} = 2000 + 500 = 2.5 \times 10^{3}$. So write both numbers with the same power of $10$, add or subtract the front numbers, then put the result back in [[standard-form|standard form]].

blocks.question: Work out $4.2 \times 10^{5} + 3.9 \times 10^{4}$. Give your answer in standard form.
steps: Rewrite the first number with the smaller power, $10^{4}$: $4.2 \times 10^{5} = 42 \times 10^{4}$.
Add the front numbers: $42 \times 10^{4} + 3.9 \times 10^{4} = 45.9 \times 10^{4}$.
Fix the front number: $45.9 = 4.59 \times 10^{1}$, so the sum is $4.59 \times 10^{5}$.
Check with ordinary numbers: $420\,000 + 39\,000 = 459\,000$, which is $4.59 \times 10^{5}$.

blocks.text: Adding the powers when you add the numbers. $3 \times 10^{4} + 2 \times 10^{4} = 5 \times 10^{4}$, not $5 \times 10^{8}$. Powers add only when you multiply.
On Paper 2 the calculator does the arithmetic. Your job is to type it in correctly and write the answer in standard form.

blocks.question: The gravitational pull between the Earth and the Moon is $F = \dfrac{G m_{1} m_{2}}{d^{2}}$ newtons, where $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$, $m_{1} = 5.97 \times 10^{24}$, $m_{2} = 7.35 \times 10^{22}$ and $d = 3.84 \times 10^{8}$. Use your calculator to find $F$. Give your answer in standard form, with $a$ to 3 s.f.
steps: Write down what you will type: $F = \dfrac{(6.67 \times 10^{-11})(5.97 \times 10^{24})(7.35 \times 10^{22})}{(3.84 \times 10^{8})^{2}}$. This line earns the method mark.
Put the whole denominator in brackets, (3.84E8)^2, so all of $d$ is squared. If you type $\times 10^{8}$ instead of E, leaving out the brackets divides by $3.84$ only.
The screen shows about 1.9848E20, which means $1.9848\ldots \times 10^{20}$.
Round the front number to 3 s.f.: $F \approx 1.98 \times 10^{20}$ N. Never write 1.98E20.

Estimate to check: $10^{-11 + 24 + 22 - 16} = 10^{19}$ and $\frac{7 \times 6 \times 7}{4 \times 4} \approx 18$, so $F$ is about $1.8 \times 10^{20}$: the same [[order-of-magnitude|order of magnitude]].

Read about 1.98484E20; the digits shown depend on your settings (check on your model)

blocks.prompt: Your calculator shows the answer 2.04E-7. How should you write it on your exam paper?
blocks.hint: E means times $10$ to the power of the number after it. Keep the sign of that number.

blocks.text: Point after the first non-zero digit; $k$ counts the places moved, negative for numbers below 1.
Multiply: multiply front numbers, add powers. Divide: divide, subtract powers. Then fix $a$.
$(a \times 10^{m})^{n} = a^{n} \times 10^{mn}$. For a square root, make the power even, then halve it.
Add or subtract only with matching powers of $10$. Compare sizes by $k$ first.
Never give 7.4E-6 as an answer. Write $7.4 \times 10^{-6}$.

mistakes: Stopping with the front number outside 1 to 10, as in $30 \times 10^{-7}$. Rewrite until $1 \le a < 10$, changing the power to balance.
Moving the power the wrong way: $52.8 \times 10^{-7}$ is $5.28 \times 10^{-6}$, not $5.28 \times 10^{-8}$. A smaller front number needs a bigger power.
Giving a number between 0 and 1 a positive power. Its $k$ is always negative: $0.0004 = 4 \times 10^{-4}$.
examTips: When standard form is asked for, $45.9 \times 10^{4}$ loses the final accuracy (A) mark: you need $1 \le a < 10$.
On Paper 1 there is no calculator. Split each calculation into front numbers and powers of $10$, and show both lines for the method (M) marks.
On Paper 2, write down the expression you type, then the answer. Round the front number to 3 s.f. unless told otherwise.
